## Finding: Missing Agent Context (crime_00017)

The scan confirms the repo ships **zero agent-readable instruction files**:

- no `AGENTS.md` at root
- no `CLAUDE.md` at root
- no `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- no `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- `package.json` declares bins (`tsup`, `tsup-node`) with no discovery path

Severity: medium, confidence: 0.9, agent_risk: 0.53.

## Why this matters for your first PR

The repo is clearly tsup (large `src/index.ts` build orchestrator, esbuild/rollup/postcss/svelte plugins, two CLI entrypoints). An agent landing cold has to **infer** all of:

- which bin to invoke (`tsup` vs `tsup-node`), and when each applies
- which package manager + test runner are canonical
- the `core` → `language-pack` → `cli` style boundaries that already exist implicitly (esbuild/rollup/postcss are separate plugin dirs — edits in one shouldn't bleed into another)
- the load-bearing files the scan already flagged: `src/utils.ts` (fan-in 18), `src/plugin.ts` (fan-in 10), `src/index.ts` (fan-out 17). These are exactly the files a confident-but-wrong agent will casually restructure on a "small" PR.

Without that context, the highest-risk failure mode isn't a broken build — it's an agent quietly refactoring `utils.ts` or splitting `index.ts` "for clarity" and breaking 18 downstream importers.

## Minimal AGENTS.md skeleton to clear the finding

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

## What this repo is
tsup — a TypeScript bundler powered by esbuild, with optional rollup-based
`.d.ts` generation. Two binaries are published: `tsup` and `tsup-node`
(the latter sets `--target node` defaults).

## Commands
- Install:  `pnpm install`
- Build:    `pnpm build`
- Test:     `pnpm test`         (vitest)
- Typecheck:`pnpm typecheck`
- Lint:     `pnpm lint`

Always run `pnpm build && pnpm test` before opening a PR.

## Layout (treat boundaries as load-bearing)
- `src/index.ts`        — main `build()` orchestrator. High fan-out; prefer additive edits.
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin lifecycle. Fan-in 10; do not restructure casually.
- `src/utils.ts`        — shared helpers. Fan-in 18; treat as a public API.
- `src/esbuild/*`       — esbuild plugins (postcss, svelte, swc). One concern per file.
- `src/rollup.ts`,
  `src/rollup/*`        — rollup config + plugins for `.d.ts` rollup only.
- `src/api-extractor.ts`— `@microsoft/api-extractor` integration for dts.
- `src/cli-main.ts`,
  `src/cli-node.ts`     — CLI entrypoints; argument parsing only, no detection logic.

## Conventions
- TypeScript everywhere; no `any` in new code.
- Side effects belong in named functions — don't add IO to anything that
  reads like a pure helper (`get*`, `build*` are watched).
- New tests must contain at least one real `expect()` — empty-body tests
  are treated as regressions.

## What NOT to do
- Don't split `src/index.ts` or `src/utils.ts` in a "small" PR — they
  have wide fan-in/out. Open an issue first.
- Don't add new top-level dependencies without justification in the PR.
- Don't introduce sync `fs.*Sync` calls in new domain code; use the
  async variants.

## Where to ask
- Issues:   https://github.com/egoist/tsup/issues
- Releases: CHANGELOG.md
```

Dropping that at the repo root would clear `crime_00017` and substantially reduce the agent_risk premium on the load-bearing files the scan flagged.
